ptxt.intxrefpoff: Main Bearing, Crankshaft and Cylinder Block Removal and Installation:K14D

attention3.ptxt: Properly use main bearings checking their width and oil hole.

entry.ptxt: Main bearing No.1 upper half with oil groove and 2 holes
Main bearing No.2 – 5 upper halves with oil groove and 1 hole

item.ptxt: Service main bearings are available in standard size and 0.25 mm (0.0098 in.) undersize, and each of them has five kinds of bearings differing in tolerance.
Upper bearing half (1) has oil groove (2) as shown in figure.
Install this half with oil groove to cylinder block.
Lower bearing half does not have oil groove.

servinfosub.title: Visual Inspection
servinfosub.ptxt: Check bearings for pitting, scratches, wear or damage.
If any defect is found, replace both upper and lower halves. Never replace either half without replacing the other half.

servinfosub.title: Main Bearing Clearance

attention3.ptxt: Do not rotate crankshaft while gauging plastic is fitted.

servinfosub.ptxt: Check clearance using gauging plastic according to the following procedure.

s1.ptxt: Remove main bearing caps.
Clean bearings and main journals.
Place a piece of gauging plastic (1) to full width of bearing (parallel to crankshaft) on journal, avoiding oil hole.
Without applying engine oil, install main bearing cap referring to Step 14) in “Installation” under Main Bearing, Crankshaft and Cylinder Block Removal and Installation:K14D .
After three minutes, remove main bearing cap and using scale (2) on gauging plastic envelope, measure gauging plastic (1) width at the widest point.

spec.title: Main bearing No.1 clearance
Main bearing No.2 – No.4clearance
Main bearing No.5 clearance

s1.ptxt: If measured clearance is less than standard or more than service limit, replace main bearings with new ones referring to Selection of Main Bearing and recheck main bearing clearance.
If measured clearance with new bearing is out of standard, select other bearing according to the following procedure and recheck main bearing clearance.

item.ptxt: Replace bearing with one size thicker or regrind crankshaft journal to undersize and use 0.25 mm (0.0098 in.) undersize bearing.
Replace bearing with one size thinner or regrind crankshaft journal to undersize and use 0.25 mm (0.0098 in.) undersize bearing.

topic.title: Standard size bearing
topic.ptxt: If engine is under one of the following conditions, select a new standard bearing as follows, and install it.

item.ptxt: Bearing clearance is out of specification.
Crankshaft or cylinder block is replaced.

s1.ptxt: Check journal diameter. As shown in figure, crank web No.4 has stamped numbers.
Six kinds of numbers (“1” – “6”) represent the following journal diameters.
Stamped numbers on crank web No.4 represent diameters of journal indicated with an arrow in figure respectively.
For example stamped number “1” indicates that corresponding journal diameter is 45.0150 – 45.0180 mm (1.77224 – 1.77236 in.).

spec.title: Crankshaft journal diameter

s1.ptxt: Check bearing cap bore diameter without bearing. On mating surface of cylinder block, five alphabets or numbers are stamped as shown in figure.
Six kinds of alphabets (“A – “F”) or numbers (“1” –”6”) represent the following journal inside diameters.
Stamped alphabet or number on cylinder block represent bearing cap bore diameter marked with an arrow in figure respectively.
For example, stamped “A” or “1” indicates that corresponding bearing cap bore diameter is 49.0000 – 49.0030 mm (1.92913 – 1.92925 in.).

spec.title: Crankshaft bearing cap bore

s1.ptxt: There are five kinds of standard bearing thickness and they are painted in the following colors.
Each color indicates the following thickness at the center of bearing.

spec.title: Standard size crankshaft upper and lower main bearing No.1 thickness
Standard size crankshaft upper main bearing No.2 – No.5 thickness
Standard size crankshaft lower main bearing No.2 – No.5 thickness

s1.ptxt: From number stamped on crank web No.4 and alphabet or number stamped on cylinder block, determine new standard bearing to be installed to journal, referring to the following table.
For example, if number stamped on crank web No.4 is “1” and alphabet stamped on cylinder block is “B”, install a new standard bearing painted in “Pink” to its journal.

s1.ptxt: Using scale (2) and gauging plastic (1), check bearing clearance with newly selected standard bearing.
If clearance still exceeds its limit, use next thicker bearing and recheck clearance, referring to Main Bearing Clearance .

item.ptxt: If necessary, regrind crankshaft journal and select undersize bearing to use with crankshaft as follows.

s1.ptxt: Regrind journal to the following finished diameter.

spec.title: Finished journal diameter

s1.ptxt: Using micrometer, measure reground journal diameter.
Measurement should be taken in two directions perpendicular to each other to check for out-of-roundness.
Using journal diameter measured above and alphabet or number stamped on cylinder block, select an undersize bearing referring to the following table.
Check bearing clearance with newly selected undersize bearing.

servinfosub.title: Main Bearing Cap Bolt
servinfosub.ptxt: Measure each thread diameter at specified points on main bearing cap bolts (1) using a micrometer (3).
If it exceeds limit, replace main bearing cap bolt with new one.
